title: OpShin Core - Developing Python Smart Contracts

ms.promise:
The Catalyst proposal outlines three tasks for the OpShin core improvements. The first one covers usability improvements: Developers should be able to perform basic operations for smart contracts easily, such as loading, deploying and interacting with them. Tooling for this (such as the support for Plutus Blueprints) is missing from OpShin and needs to be implemented

Concrete outputs should include:
・Support for Plutus Blueprints (https://github.com/OpShin/opshin/issues/57)
・Support for transaction building with OpShin (https://github.com/OpShin/uplc/issues/12)
・Better error reporting and logging (https://github.com/OpShin/opshin/issues/160)
ms.criteria: The three marked issues (Support for Plutus Blueprints, Support for transaction building with OpShin, Better error reporting and logging) should be converted into Pull Requests (PR) with corresponding code changes. This means that the developers will publicly share what changes they have made to the codebase to resolve the given issues. As usually done, there will also be a verbatim explanation of each PR through the Twitter Page (@OpShinDev) of the main project.

ms.promise:
The Catalyst proposal outlines three tasks for the OpShin core improvements. The third one covers simulation: The Plutus VM needs to be fully implemented in Python in order to give full freedom and flexibility when developing in a Python stack on Cardano. The current implementation is lacking precision and testing as well as primitives that will be present in Plutus V3.
A fully typesafe and cost-measuring implementation of the Plutus VM in Python.
Related issues include
・Natively evaluate Tx in UPLC (https://github.com/OpShin/uplc/issues/12)
・Check types for builtins (https://github.com/OpShin/uplc/issues/4)
